patches.reason: inspect.getargspec was removed in Python 3.11; models/model_interface.py and datasets/data_interface.py call it in instancialize() and read only .args, which inspect.getfullargspec returns unchanged.

models/TransMIL.py:73 moves the class token to CUDA; the reference runs on the CPU (lab answer cpu_fp32_patched), so Tensor.cuda returns the tensor itself without changing values or the autograd graph.

The shipped config trains with precision 16 / amp_level O2 on GPU (--gpus default [2]). The reference is CPU FP32 (lab answer cpu_fp32_patched): precision 32, amp_level None and gpus None are passed to the original Trainer call.

The config uses 8 DataLoader worker processes; the confined single-thread run loads batches in the main process. Sampler order and the torch base-seed draw are made in the main process either way, and data_shuffle is False, so values and order are unchanged.

The original load_loggers still runs (it sets cfg.log_path used by the callbacks and the test stage), but its TensorBoard/CSV logger constructors are replaced by no-ops (tensorboard is not installed) and no logger is given to the Trainer; logging does not affect training. EarlyStopping and ModelCheckpoint stay active because they implement the original model selection.
pytorch-lightning 1.9.5 (EarlyStopping and ModelCheckpoint initial best scores) reads np.Inf, which NumPy 2 removed; the alias is the same float numpy.inf.

nystrom-attention 0.0.9 splits to_qkv(x) with chunk(), rearranges each part to heads and then scales q in place (q *= self.scale); torch >= 1.8 (here 2.11) raises on in-place edits of multi-output views (torch 1.7 only warned). Inside that module the 'b n (h d) -> b h n d' rearrange result is cloned: forward values are identical and the clone's backward is the identity, so the gradient is the correct gradient of the same graph.

torch 2.11 wraps Optimizer subclasses' step() with hook dispatch that reads the hook registries created in Optimizer.__init__; MyOptimizer/lookahead.py's Lookahead does not call Optimizer.__init__. Empty registries are added to the class; no hook is registered, so the step computation is unchanged.

torch >= 2.6 loads checkpoints with weights_only=True by default; the test stage's load_from_checkpoint (train.py:76) reads the checkpoint the train stage just wrote, whose saved hyperparameters contain addict.Dict, which that loader cannot rebuild. TORCH_FORCE_NO_WEIGHTS_ONLY_LOAD=1 is set before the test stage only, restoring the torch 1.x full-unpickle default; the loaded weights are unchanged.
